subject: SpeedScale: latency vs batching — post-demo decision matrix
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@speedscale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T15:10:00Z
Subject: SpeedScale: latency vs batching — post-demo decision matrix

Tom — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our side so we can align on whether Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, or Private VPC is the right path for SpeedScale. I captured the runtime signals you shared and our initial recommendation.

Summary of what we heard from your team:
- P95 latency requirement for interactive UI: <= 120ms for short prompts (~64 tokens).
- Peak concurrent QPS: 120 requests/sec during traffic spikes, baseline ~30 QPS.
- Some long-running generation for analytical reports (avg 800 tokens) that can tolerate 1–2s latency.
- Data residency: US-only, but not strictly air-gapped; audit logs required.

Initial qualification matrix (tradeoffs):
1) Hosted API
  - Pros: fastest onboarding, automatic global routing, built-in streaming. Good if you accept small variance in tail latency and rely on our caching/batching to reduce cost.
  - Cons: shared pools could produce higher tail latency at 120 QPS spikes without burst reservations.
2) Dedicated capacity
  - Pros: predictable tail latency SLOs, reserved GPU pools for sustained 120 QPS, can tune batching strategies and run quantized models for cost.
  - Cons: longer provisioning lead time; higher fixed cost at low baseline.
3) Private VPC/on-prem
  - Pros: full control for logs/KMS and strict audit requirements.
  - Cons: operational overhead and slower iteration.

Recommendation: run a 2-week pilot on Dedicated capacity configured with a burst window and prefix caching for interactive endpoints, and route heavy analytic jobs to Hosted for cost efficiency. This gives predictable p95 for the UI while letting you leverage Hosted for non-latency‑sensitive workloads.

Next steps (proposed):
- Redwood: provide a latency/QPS tuning playbook + sample batch settings (we attach a latency-qps-matrix.xlsx).
- SpeedScale: confirm a 2-week pilot window and nominate an internal owner for load testing (we suggest Nov 23–Dec 7).
- Legal/Procurement: high-level T&Cs review for Dedicated listing (we can send a streamlined SOW).

Attachments: speedscale-demo-recording.mp4 (30m call recording), latency-qps-matrix.xlsx (initial tuning grid).

If that sounds good, we'll schedule a short ROI/ops alignment with Marissa and Ben present.

Thanks,
Karthik

Subject: Re: SpeedScale: latency vs batching — post-demo decision matrix

Thanks, Karthik — this is very helpful. Quick answers from our side:
- We can nominate Priya Anand as the load-testing owner (cc'ed on my reply).
- Nov 23–Dec 7 pilot window works for us.
- We want to avoid ops-heavy private deployment for now; leaning toward Dedicated + some Hosted for batch.

Two items we need clarified before we commit:
1) On Dedicated, what padding (headroom) do you recommend for 120 QPS spikes? Do you suggest a 20% buffer or a larger reserve?
2) For the interactive endpoint, can you confirm the expected p95 tail under your recommended batching config (we shared token distribution in the call)?

I'll review the attached matrix after this note.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@speedscale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Anand <priya@speedscale.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T20:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SpeedScale: latency vs batching — post-demo decision matrix

Tom / Priya — answers inline:
1) Headroom recommendation: we typically design for 1.25x sustained headroom for GPUs handling prefix-heavy interactive traffic (so 25% buffer). For short-burst unpredicted events we enable burst capacity (separate burst pool) that can cover up to 1.6x for short durations (minutes). That keeps costs reasonable while avoiding provisioning for worst-case sustained load.

2) Expected p95: with Dedicated + prefix KV caching and conservative batching (max batch 8, 40ms batching window), we expect p95 in the 90–120ms range for ~64-token prompts on A100-class instances with model quantization enabled. We'll validate this with a test harness during pilot. Hosted for the same configuration typically shows higher tail variance (p95 could stretch to 150–220ms under shared peak).

Operational notes:
- We'll instrument token-level tracing and include a per-route cost/latency dashboard in the pilot so you can watch p95 and tail in near real-time.
- Marissa will propose a Dedicated sizing and pricing estimate once you confirm pilot dates.

I've uploaded a short runbook and the tuning grid to the Drive link. If you want, Ben can run a brief loadtest kickoff with your infra team next week to sanity check traffic profiles.

Best,
Karthik
